subModules.title: Reading Mission: Ongoing Operations and System Updates
subModules.grammarFocus: Present Continuous and Present Perfect Passives
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Manufacturing, Office Renovations, and System Maintenance

content.summary: Welcome to your reading mission. Today, you will explore how factories, offices, and computer systems are managed, renovated, and upgraded. You will learn to recognize the passive voice when focusing on actions that are happening right now or actions that have just been completed. By reading authentic descriptions of workplace operations, you will strengthen your ability to understand formal reports and status updates.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Present Continuous Passive (is/are being + V3) and Present Perfect Passive (has/have been + V3)
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Verbs related to manufacturing, construction, inspection, and system updates
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming texts for general workflow updates and scanning for specific operational status details

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short B1 texts about factory and office updates.
Locate specific details regarding ongoing operations and completed tasks.
Recognize and interpret passive structures in Present Continuous and Present Perfect tenses.

contextWarmup.prompt: When an office building is undergoing repairs, what is the most important message for employees to receive?
options: Details about which areas are being renovated and when the work will finish
A history of architecture in the local city
Instructions on how to bake a cake in the breakroom
contextWarmup.explanation: In workplace updates, employees need practical information about ongoing renovations and timelines so they can plan their workday safely.

rules: Present Continuous Passive: is/are being + past participle (V3). Example: The factory is being renovated.
Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle (V3). Example: New security cameras have been installed.
Use Present Continuous Passive for actions happening right now, and Present Perfect Passive for actions completed with current relevance.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners sometimes see 'is being' or 'has been' and forget that the subject receives the action rather than performs it.
commonTrap.wrong: The computers are being upgraded the IT team. (Incorrect agent preposition)
commonTrap.correct: The computers are being upgraded by the IT team.

content.passageTitle: Behind the Scenes at Apex Global Operations
paragraphs: Welcome to Apex Global Operations, where exciting changes are happening every single day. Right now, the main headquarters building is being renovated to provide better spaces for our growing teams. On the third floor, new meeting rooms are being constructed, and modern glass walls are being fitted by our contractors. At the same time, safety procedures are being implemented across all departments to ensure everyone works in a secure environment. Every piece of heavy machinery is being inspected thoroughly before morning shifts begin.

In addition to physical renovations, our technology infrastructure has undergone major improvements this quarter. All computer systems have been upgraded to the latest operating software, and fast security firewalls have been installed by the IT department. Furthermore, all staff members have been notified about the new digital workflows via email. Customer orders are being processed rapidly, and thousands of finished goods have been dispatched to international clients this week. Management has authorized these updates to keep Apex Global at the forefront of the industry.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Office Renovations and System Updates

content.summary: This briefing covers how to listen for ongoing and completed actions using present continuous and present perfect passive structures. Pay attention to how speakers emphasize actions happening right now versus actions that were recently finished.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about office changes and renovations.
Identify details such as delivery statuses and work progress.
Notice how words link together in connected speech during natural conversations.

keyPhrases.note: Used to describe an action happening right now to a building or room.
Used when an action is completed before the present moment with a focus on the result.
Shows that an installation process is currently in progress.
Highlights the successful finish of a task or project.

connectedSpeech.note: The consonant sound at the end of are links smoothly into being.
The auxiliary verb have is often unstressed in fast spoken English.
The double l sound merges into the s of staff.
The plural z sound connects directly to the b of being.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Passive Voice in Ongoing Operations

content.summary: Practical guide on using Present Continuous Passive and Present Perfect Passive to describe ongoing manufacturing processes, system updates, and completed actions in professional writing.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Present Continuous Passive Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Object + is / are + being + past participle (V3) (+ by agent)
blueprintItems.example: The factory is being renovated this month.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Present Perfect Passive Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Object + has / have + been + past participle (V3) (+ by agent)
blueprintItems.example: All safety reports have been submitted to the manager.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Choosing the Correct Aspect for Operations
blueprintItems.formula: Use Continuous for current actions and Perfect for recently finished tasks with current results.
blueprintItems.example: The software is being updated now, and new security patches have been installed.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always include 'being' between the verb 'to be' and the past participle in Present Continuous Passive.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The new cars are built in the factory right now.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The new cars are being built in the factory right now.
mechanicsRules.why: The word 'being' shows that the action is happening at the present moment.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'has been' for singular objects and 'have been' for plural objects in Present Perfect Passive.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The documents has been signed by the director.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The documents have been signed by the director.
mechanicsRules.why: Plural nouns require the plural auxiliary verb 'have'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize the first letter of every sentence and keep professional terminology consistent.
mechanicsRules.badExample: the shipment is being prepared for delivery.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The shipment is being prepared for delivery.
mechanicsRules.why: Standard English punctuation requires starting every sentence with a capital letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this active sentence into a Present Continuous Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Workers are painting the office walls today.
targetAnswers: The office walls are being painted today.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In Present Continuous Passive, the object (the office walls) becomes the subject, followed by 'are being' and the past participle 'painted'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this active sentence into a Present Perfect Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The supervisor has approved all vacation requests.
targetAnswers: All vacation requests have been approved.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The plural object 'all vacation requests' requires 'have been' followed by the past participle 'approved'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the error in this Present Continuous Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The report is write by the team right now.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'write' to the past participle form.
targetAnswers: The report is being written by the team right now.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present Continuous Passive requires 'is/are being' plus the past participle (written), not the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the error in this Present Perfect Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The new software have been installed on every computer.
practicumQuestions.hint: Check the agreement between the singular subject and the auxiliary verb.
targetAnswers: The new software has been installed on every computer.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The noun 'software' is singular in English, so it requires 'has been' instead of 'have been'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct Present Continuous Passive form:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Look! The damaged bridge ______ (repair) by the workers.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because the subject 'The damaged bridge' is singular and the action is happening now, use 'is being repaired'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct Present Perfect Passive form:
practicumQuestions.promptText: All safety guidelines ______ (update) for the new year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The plural subject 'All safety guidelines' combined with a completed action requires 'have been updated'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rearrange these words into a correct Present Continuous Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: building / new / the / is / constructed / being
targetAnswers: The new building is being constructed.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The correct order is Subject (The new building) + auxiliary (is) + being + past participle (constructed).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rearrange these words into a correct Present Perfect Passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.explanation: The correct order is Subject (The documents) + auxiliary (have been) + past participle (signed).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a Present Continuous Passive sentence describing what is happening to your car at the garage:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Car status: Repair in progress at the garage.
targetAnswers: My car is being repaired at the garage.
The car is being repaired at the garage.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To describe an ongoing action on an object, use the Present Continuous Passive structure (is being repaired).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a Present Perfect Passive sentence stating that the weekly newsletter has been sent out:
targetAnswers: The newsletter has been sent to subscribers.
Weekly newsletter has been sent to subscribers.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To describe a completed task with current results, use the Present Perfect Passive structure (has been sent).

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Passive Voice in Ongoing Operations

content.summary: Master speaking about active operations and system updates using Present Continuous and Present Perfect passive structures. Focus on linking auxiliary verbs like is being, are being, has been, and have been smoothly with main past participles to sound professional.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to weak forms of auxiliary verbs. In spoken English, words like 'been' and 'being' are often pronounced with reduced vowel sounds unless you need to emphasize completion or ongoing status.

pillars.name: Auxiliary Reduction
pillars.explanation: Reduce 'been' to /bɪn/ and blend it naturally into the past participle.

pillars.name: Stress on Action Verbs
pillars.target: Clear syllable stress on main content verbs
pillars.explanation: Place primary stress on the past participle such as in-STALLED, re-NO-va-ted, or man-u-FAC-tured.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the main stress shifts to the third syllable when changing from the verb to the noun form.
Stress moves to the third syllable in the longer noun form.
The stress stays on the second syllable for both verb and noun.
The primary stress remains on the first syllable in both the base verb and the past participle.

practicumQuestions.targetSentence: These smartphones are being manufactured in our new factory.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðiːz ˈsmɑːnfəʊnz ɑː ˈbiːɪŋ ˈmænfəktʃərd ɪn ˈaʊə nuː ˈfæktəri/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Place primary stress on the second syllable of 'manufactured'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence aloud using a rising intonation on the question part, if applicable, or falling intonation for a clear statement of completion.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence clearly: Your order has been dispatched and will arrive tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Your order has been dispatched and will arrive tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /jɔːr ˈɔːdə hæz biːn dɪˈspætʃt ænd wɪl əˈraɪv təˈmɒrəʊ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use falling intonation at the end of the sentence to show a complete, confident statement.
